name: Rocca
workload: AEAD encryption throughput (Gbps) over inputs of 64-16384 bytes with 13 bytes of associated data, benchmarked against OpenSSL 3.1.0-dev's AES-256-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 plus SNOW-V-GCM, AEGIS-128/128L/256 and Tiaoxin-346
claimed_speedup: 150.95 Gbps (Rocca AEAD) vs 29.08 Gbps AES-256-GCM (~5.2x) and 7.60 Gbps ChaCha20-Poly1305 (~19.9x) at 16384 bytes on Intel Core i7-1068NG7 (paper Table 7); up to 235.45 Gbps vs 44.82 Gbps AES-256-GCM (~5.3x, derived from page data) on i9-12900K (paper Appendix Table 8)
hardware: Intel Core i7-1068NG7 @ 2.30GHz, 32GB RAM (primary Table 7); also i9-12900K, i9-11900, i9-10910 in Appendix A
stars_or_usage: 5 stars (ericlagergren/rocca implementation); algorithm published in IACR Trans. Symmetric Cryptol. (ToSC) 2022/1, extended from FSE 2021
tradeoffs: 256-bit key, 128-bit tag; needs AES-NI+SSE3 (x86) or Crypto+NEON (ARMv8) to hit these speeds, falls back slow otherwise; far less cryptanalysis than AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305; no nonce-misuse resistance; the closely related Rocca-S variant has since had practical committing-attack weaknesses published
caveats: The benchmark is run by the algorithm's own authors (paper Table 7/Appendix A), not an independent third party, though it directly measures OpenSSL's own AES-256-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305 implementations rather than reference numbers from elsewhere; exact compiler and optimization flags are not stated (only that _mm_aesenc_si128/_mm_xor_si128 intrinsics were used), which caps the tier at B; the ericlagergren/rocca repo is an independent, unofficial C/ASM port that has been dormant since early 2022
found_via: SUPERCOP eBACS AEAD benchmark fastest implementations -> gh search code 'Rocca aesenc' -> IACR ePrint 2022/116 (Rocca: An Efficient AES-based Encryption Scheme for Beyond 5G) Table 7 and Appendix A

name: Rocca-S
workload: AEAD encryption/decryption throughput at 64KB messages, 4096-byte-aligned buffers, key/nonce setup included, no associated data beyond default framing
claimed_speedup: ROCCA-S AEAD encryption 208.1 Gbps vs AES-128-GCM 70.8 Gbps (~2.9x) at 64KB on Apple Silicon M5 Max (Apple clang 21.0.0, OpenSSL 3.6.4); 174.6 Gbps AEAD encryption on AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' (clang 21.1.8, -O3 -march=native, OpenSSL 3.5.5, AES-GCM figure not broken out for that CPU in the same table)
hardware: Apple Silicon M5 Max, macOS 26; AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' fixed at 3.8GHz, performance governor, turbo/frequency-scaling disabled
stars_or_usage: 21 stars (jedisct1/zig-rocca-s); algorithm specified in IETF draft-nakano-rocca-s, designed for 6G by NICT/KDDI-affiliated researchers
tradeoffs: 256-bit key, 256-bit tag; decryption is up to ~1.9x slower than encryption because the message block is only recoverable after an AES round completes, unlike AEGIS; requires AES-NI/ARM crypto extensions; practical committing-attack weaknesses have been published against Rocca-S (IACR ePrint 2024/901)
caveats: Numbers cited come from a third-party benchmark repo (hiae-aead/benchmarks) that bundles its own reference copy of Rocca-S rather than jedisct1's port, though both implement the same published algorithm and should perform comparably; jedisct1's own repo README separately reports 189.78 Gbps on Apple M4 but without a same-repo AES-GCM comparison
found_via: SUPERCOP eBACS AEAD benchmark fastest implementations -> gh search repos 'ascon'/'AEAD benchmark' -> hiae-aead/benchmarks shootout README (harvested ROCCA-S and HiAE results)

name: HiAE
workload: AEAD encryption/decryption throughput at 64KB messages, 4096-byte-aligned buffers, key/nonce setup included
claimed_speedup: HiAE AEAD encryption 266.7 Gbps vs AES-128-GCM 70.8 Gbps (~3.8x) at 64KB on Apple Silicon M5 Max (Apple clang 21.0.0, OpenSSL 3.6.4); 268.4 Gbps AEAD encryption on AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' (clang 21.1.8, -O3 -march=native, OpenSSL 3.5.5)
hardware: Apple Silicon M5 Max, macOS 26; AMD Ryzen 7 7700 'Zen 4' fixed at 3.8GHz, performance governor, turbo/frequency-scaling disabled
tradeoffs: Decryption up to ~1.93x slower than encryption on Zen4 (message block only recoverable after an AES round, same asymmetry class as Rocca-S); multi-lane HiAEx2/HiAEx4 variants trade some single-stream throughput for AVX-512/VAES parallelism
caveats: This is a Tier A independent benchmark (compiler, flags and CPU model all stated, code public) for a project already on the excluded/known list (concyclics/hiae); reported here as supplementary evidence per the is_evidence_for_known exception rather than as a new catalog entry. GitHub detects no license file for concyclics/hiae, so usability is recorded as reference pending confirmation
found_via: SUPERCOP eBACS AEAD benchmark fastest implementations -> gh search repos 'AEAD benchmark' -> hiae-aead/benchmarks (angt/hiae-bench-results mirror of the same suite)

name: LeMac
baseline: GHASH (the universal-hash MAC component of OpenSSL AES-GCM)
workload: Universal-hash/MAC throughput per 128-bit message block, 2 AES-round calls per block
claimed_speedup: 0.068 cycles/byte on Intel Ice Lake, described by the authors as a 60% throughput improvement over the state-of-the-art AES-based universal hash function (abstract does not name GHASH specifically or give its own cycles/byte)
hardware: Intel Ice Lake (exact CPU model, RAM and compiler not stated in the abstract)
stars_or_usage: 2 stars (reference implementation repo); algorithm published IACR Trans. Symmetric Cryptol. (ToSC) 2024/2
tradeoffs: LeMac is a MAC/universal-hash primitive, not a complete AEAD; it must be paired with a stream cipher (e.g. AES-CTR) to form a full AES-GCM replacement, so it cannot be dropped in on its own; a sibling construction (LeMac-0) had a message-schedule bug in the original paper, fixed in this repo; CC0-1.0 dedication carries no patent grant
caveats: The abstract's speedup is versus an unnamed 'state-of-the-art' AES-based universal hash function, not an explicitly named comparison to OpenSSL's GHASH; no compiler, exact CPU model, or flags are given, so this is capped at Tier B with reduced confidence; the companion benchmark suite in the same repo (which also builds GCM, Rocca, Rocca-S, HiAE, AEGIS and Tiaoxin from source) ships no pre-generated results, only a script to run locally
found_via: SUPERCOP eBACS AEAD benchmark fastest implementations -> found via 'Rocca: reference code from the ePrint paper' cross-reference inside AugustinBariant/Implementations_LeMac_PetitMac benchmark README -> IACR ToSC article 11619
